data.segment_title: Preview/Introduction Tom Brokaw (Republican National Convention in New York)
Campaign 2004 / Bush vs. Kerry / Republican Convention / Protests
data.segment_description:
(New York: Tom Brokaw)  Aerial view of a massive protest in New York City against President Bush's Iraq policy shown. 
 (New York: Tom Costello)  The protests in the streets of New York City the day before the Republican National Convention featured; scenes shown of the massive chanting crowd in Manhattan demonstrating against the war in Iraq & Bush & of police making arrests.  [Speakers Jesse JACKSON, filmmaker Michael MOORE†, DEMONSTRATORS&nbsp- speak out.] 
 (Manhattan: Ron Allen)  The Manhattan protests by the coalition group United for Peace & Justice featured; scenes shown of the parade-like protest against the war & other issues.  [Protesters New Yorker Eric LUSTIG, Floridian Melissa QUESTERIE, Gray Panther Judy LEAR, Teachers for Peace Jackie PARKS, New Jerseyites Bob & Maxine COLE&nbsp- outline their protests.] 
 (New York: Tom Brokaw)  Report introduced. 
 (New York: Chip Reid)  The start of the convention by Vice President Dick Cheney & President Bush's campaigning featured; scenes shown of him at Madison Square Garden.  [Earlier on Ellis Island, CHENEY&nbsp- speaks about President Bush at Ground Zero after September 11.]  [BUSH&nbsp- recalls September 11.]  [Bush campaign advisor Karen HUGHES†- says Bush needs another four year to make the world a better place.] 
 (New York: Tom Brokaw)  Report introduced. 
 (New York: Carl Quintanilla)  The message for Democrats from former President Bill Clinton & Senator Hillary Clinton on the eve of the Republican convention presented.  [At a Manhattan church, Bill CLINTON&nbsp- jokes about the Republicans.]  [On "Meet the Press," Hillary CLINTON&nbsp- defends Senator John Kerry.]  [Democratic spokesman Matt BENNETT†- comments.]  Bush's statement in "Time" magazine in which he calls Iraq a "catastrophic success" noted.  [Senator John EDWARDS&nbsp- reacts to Bush's statement.]  [Analyst Charlie COOK&nbsp- says Kerry will campaign during the opponent's convention.] 
 (New York: Tom Brokaw)  NBC's exclusive interview with Bush noted.
(New York: Tom Brokaw)  The arrival of Tropical Storm Gaston on the Carolina coast reported; rain scenes shown.

(New York: Tom Brokaw)  A car bombing in Kabul, Afghanistan, that targeted an American security firm's building reported; scenes shown; details given of efforts to disrupt Afghanistan's scheduled elections.

(New York: Tom Brokaw)  Report introduced. 
 (Moscow: Dawna Friesen)  The presidential elections in the violent, lawless Chechnya, Russia, examined; scenes shown of the May assassination of the last Chechen president, Akhmad Kadyrov††; details given about the pro-Russian candidate & last week's bombing of two Russian planes.  [Human rights advocate Malcolm HAWKES†- says the Chechen elections are not credible; notes over 100 deaths last week.]  [Russian political analyst Masha LIPMAN†- comments on the assassination in spite of Kadyrov having his own army.]

(New York: Tom Brokaw)  Findings of the latest NBC News/"Wall Street Journal" poll on the 2004 election & whether the removal of Iraqi President Saddam Hussein was worth the cost & on the economy & the war on terrorism outlined on screen. 
 (New York: Andrea Mitchell)  The Republicans' strategy for the convention that opens tomorrow previewed; details given about how Bush will appeal to the independent voter, his stance on the economic issues, how to handle events in Iraq & Afghanistan & the emphasis on drama to make Bush appear more likeable.

(New York: Tom Brokaw)  Report introduced. 
 (Athens: Lester Holt)  The spectacular end of the Olympic Games in Athens, Greece, reviewed; photos shown; scenes shown of the bizarre incident during the marathon when Brazilian runner Vanderlei de Lima†† was interfered with by an intruder who turned out to be a costumed defrocked Irish priest.  The overall medal count reviewed. 
 (Baltimore: Roger O'Neill)  American Olympic swimmers as role models for the young featured; scenes shown from the Olympic pool & from Baltimore.  [Young swimmer Joe HEALY‡- cites Olympic swimmer Michael Phelps.]  [1976 medal-winning swimmer Bruce FURNISS‡, 2004 swimmer Ian CROCKER, his grandmother Phyllis CROCKER, young swimmer Kelsey BOYER&nbsp- comment on the Olympic team experience.] 
 (Athens: Lester Holt)  The coming winter Olympic Games in Italy in 2006 & the summer games in Beijing, China, in 2008 noted.
